papers_new.title: Resolving and Suppressing Temporally Correlated Noise in Quantum Error Correction
papers_new.abstract: Scaling fault-tolerant quantum error correction (QEC) requires suppressing errors in both space and time, yet standard logical memory experiments primarily probe spatial faults. Here, we use a 105-qubit Willow superconducting quantum processor to realize and scale the surface code stability experiment, which is alternatively sensitive to temporal error chains. Scaling from patch sizes of $3 \times 3$ to $7 \times 7$, we realize a timelike block suppression factor of $μ_T = 1.47 \pm 0.25$, demonstrating the ability to maintain temporal error suppression as the number of qubits increases. By extending the stability experiment for many cycles, we uncover a sum-of-exponentials behavior in error suppression caused by a temporally correlated error: data-qubit heating to the third excited state $|3\rangle$. We fully capture this effect with a parameter-free, device-level leakage model…

papers_new.title: Rate-1/2 Quantum LDPC Codes for Multi-tier Superconducting Hardware
papers_new.abstract: Quantum error correction is essential for scalable quantum computing, while its resource overhead is governed in large part by the encoding rate, namely the number of logical qubits encoded per physical data qubit. Recent quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) constructions have entered the ultra-high-rate regime with encoding rates above 1/2, but their syndrome-extraction circuits generally rely on reconfigurable connectivity or long-range qubit transport, making them difficult to implement on fixed-connectivity superconducting hardware. Here we introduce Armillary codes, a family of ultra-high-rate qLDPC codes whose algebraic structure is generated by native iSWAP routing under hardware constraints. The construction jointly enforces stabilizer commutation and correct parallel syndrome extraction, while admitting radial and circumferential couplings in crossing-free routing layers.…

papers_new.title: Proxima: Optimizing Syndrome Extraction Circuit Scheduling for Practical Quantum LDPC Codes
papers_new.abstract: The fault-tolerant performance of quantum error correction codes relies critically on the scheduling of parity checks in syndrome extraction circuits (SECs). For general CSS-type quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes, the vast scheduling space and intricate error-propagation patterns make it computationally prohibitive to directly optimize the logical error rate (LER) or the exact circuit-level distance ($d_{\mathrm{circ}}$). To address this challenge, we introduce Proxima, a highly effective automated SEC scheduling framework guided by a distance-related metric termed proximity. Defined directly on the detector error model (DEM), proximity quantifies the minimum number of additional faults required to complete a seed fault to an undetectable logical failure, naturally capturing arbitrary circuit-level fault mechanisms and bounding $d_{\mathrm{circ}}$ from above. Proxima…
papers_new.excerpt: The fault-tolerant performance of quantum error correction codes relies critically on the scheduling of parity checks in syndrome extraction circuits (SECs).

papers_new.title: Hierarchical Decoding for Quantum Error Correction
papers_new.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires classical decoders that can keep up with syndrome data streams and supply correction information and logical measurement outcomes to the quantum control system. Meeting these requirements at scale requires high throughput while controlling the end-to-end latency from readout to usable correction. In this paper, we organize decoding algorithms, execution strategies, and code constructions using common classifications and examine their performance and trade-offs under the reported evaluation conditions. We distinguish decoder-level hierarchy, where multiple decoding stages or resources cooperate to decode a single code, from code-level hierarchy, where the code construction itself introduces multiple decoding levels. We first review single-code hierarchical decoders and their cascaded predecoding and windowed, streaming, and distributed…
papers_new.excerpt: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires classical decoders that can keep up with syndrome data streams and supply correction information and logical measurement outcomes to the quantum control system.

papers_new.title: An Architecture for Real-Time Quantum Error Correction with Neutral Atoms
papers_new.abstract: The latency of quantum measurement and classical decoding constrains the execution of adaptive fault-tolerant circuits. In neutral-atom processors, this requirement couples spatially resolved fluorescence detection to classical inference. Here we implement cascaded readout and decoding in a heterogeneous architecture that overlaps acquisition and processing at two spatial scales. Field-programmable gate arrays process camera rows as they arrive, while graphics processors decode an acquired logical block during acquisition of the next. This heterogeneous architecture offers flexibility in the choice of error-correcting codes and decoding algorithms. Direct communication preserves microsecond-scale transfer times for kilobyte payloads and supports interchangeable decoding algorithms. papers_new.title: Machine-learning decoders for fusion-based quantum computing in real time
papers_new.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires decoders that combine accuracy, throughput, low latency, and scalability to large numbers of physical qubits. In photonic fusion-based architectures, erasures from photon loss and probabilistic fusion measurements are a dominant error mechanism, motivating decoders that remain accurate at high erasure rates. We introduce PRISM, a transformer-based machine-learning decoder designed to exploit the known locations of erasures in protocols subject to both Pauli and erasure errors. We benchmark PRISM across a wide range of fault-tolerant protocols based on surface codes, color codes, and quantum low-density parity-check codes, with distances up to 24. Across these benchmarks, PRISM matches the logical error rates of integer-programming-based decoders while being significantly faster, including at error rates up to 50% of threshold. We further…

papers_new.title: How wide must an eavesdropper be? Leakage of a toric-code logical bit to a strip and the Nishimori point
papers_new.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computers hand pieces of each logical qubit to separate decoder modules and shared readout lines. How much does a piece reveal? We prove that for any region and any Pauli noise, including correlated noise, an observer's optimal advantage in learning a logical bit is exactly 1 - 2 P_fail, where P_fail is the failure probability of maximum-likelihood decoding confined to that region. Two lessons follow. Geometry, not noise, provides the protection: a region that misses a single column of the code learns exactly nothing at any noise level, while a region that spans the code is protected by noise only at impractical distances (d > 350 for one row at a 10^-3 flip rate). And width is a poor guide to risk: under i.i.d. noise a two-row strip learns exactly as little as one row, yet below threshold an eavesdropper needs a width growing only as ln d. papers_new.title: Magic state cultivation with lattice-surgery escape on superconducting hardware
papers_new.abstract: Magic state cultivation (MSC) is a low-overhead protocol for fault-tolerantly preparing logical magic states. In this work, we implement two MSC variants to prepare a magic state in a distance-5 code on a publicly available IBM Nighthawk processor. The first is a lattice-surgery escape, recently proposed by Hirano et al. and experimentally studied here for the first time. The second is a grafting escape, previously demonstrated by Rosenfeld et al., and extended here by incorporating a switch into a matchable code. Both protocols begin with fault-tolerant cultivation of a T state on a color code, followed by an escape into a larger code. We decode the results using minimum-weight perfect matching or Tesseract on circuit-level error models calibrated to the hardware noise. Compared with the previous experiment, our cultivated T state achieves a logical error probability of 2e-5 at the…

papers_new.title: Probing the real-time decoding accuracy bounds in trapped ion architectures
papers_new.abstract: Fault tolerant quantum computers will rely on real-time decoders that process syndromes faster than the QEC cycle duration. The millisecond cycle times offered by trapped ion platforms relax low-latency decoding demands, but simulations and experiments have not yet exploited this time budget to reach maximum logical error suppression. We show how a hybrid sliding window decoding scheme composed of a lower-accuracy and a higher-accuracy decoder can yield substantially improved logical error rates, while preserving low latency. All windows are handled by the lower-accuracy decoder, with some windows being infrequently switched to the higher-accuracy decoder. We extract soft-output information from the lower-accuracy decoder efficiently for any QLDPC code, which allows us to identify decoding windows of low confidence. papers_new.title: Exponential Quantum Memory Advantage for Late-Graph Smoothness and Spectral Estimation
papers_new.abstract: Graph signal processing tests how smoothly the decisions of next-generation massive sensor networks with $N$ nodes vary over their neighbour graph. Memory becomes the bottleneck when the neighbour graph arrives only after data erasure, a late-graph setting motivated by dispersed sensor networks and telemetry. We analyse three collection scenarios, reliable rounds, continuous broadcast and ordered capture, and test the Dirichlet energy $\mathcal E_G=\mathbf z^{\mathsf T}\mathbf L\mathbf z/N$ of the fused decision map $\mathbf z\in\{\pm1\}^N$, with late-graph Laplacian $\mathbf L$, against two thresholds. Hidden Matching uses $O(\log N)$ qubits on fused bits, but in reliable rounds and continuous broadcast, where nodes report $b$ sub-bits separately, a classical record buffer before it uses $O(N b)$ bits; classical methods need $Ω(\sqrt N)$ bits in the worst case. papers_new.title: TCBP-JOBS: GPU-Accelerated Quantum Error Correction Decoding and Noise Learning with Near-Optimal Accuracy
papers_new.abstract: Achieving near-optimal quantum error correction (QEC) decoding accuracy often requires computationally expensive searches that limit both large-scale simulation and real-time operation. We introduce trajectory-calibrated belief propagation (TCBP), which learns calibrated fault probabilities from BP trajectories, and jittered OSD beam search (JOBS), which uses these probabilities to guide parallel GPU searches. Across surface, color and bivariate-bicycle code memory and surgery circuits, TCBP-JOBS achieves logical error rates comparable to those of the Tesseract most-likely-error decoder at physical error rates of 0.1% to 0.4%, and up to 4.5$\times$ lower on the largest codes. papers_new.title: Closing the loop on memory: accurate, shallow and transferable decoding of quantum LDPC codes
papers_new.abstract: Quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes have attracted interest for fault-tolerant quantum computing because their high-rate constructions offer a route to reduced qubit overhead. Realizing this potential requires reliable decoding. Belief propagation (BP) forms the basis of many qLDPC decoders, but can fail to converge under circuit-level noise. Memory-based variants can improve convergence, yet selecting memory strengths that work reliably across different syndromes remains challenging. Here we introduce TEMPO-BP, which adapts each variable's memory strength to the evolving decoding state through local feedback. On the gross code at a physical error rate of 0.4%, single-run TEMPO-BP achieves a per-shot logical failure rate of 0.73%, compared with 2.51% for BP+OSD+CS-10. papers_new.title: Accurate qLDPC decoding under real-time constraints
papers_new.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires reconciling the computational demands of accurate decoding with the stringent timing constraints of real-time error correction. We present Spatiotemporal Covariance-Optimized Parallel Ensemble (SCOPE), a physics-informed framework for real-time decoding of quantum low-density parity-check codes (qLDPC). By exploiting the spatial symmetries of bivariate-bicycle (BB) codes and the temporal regularity of repeated syndrome extraction, SCOPE uncovers a spatiotemporally covariant decoding structure and organizes the circuit-level problem into a layered decoding strategy. We further compress the high-dimensional evolution of belief propagation (BP) into a low-dimensional dynamical representation, revealing distinct signatures of successful and failed decoding and enabling early detection of unpromising trajectories. papers_new.title: Scaling Pêlagos: Multi-GPU Orchestration for Relay Belief-Propagation Decoding
papers_new.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires quantum error-correction (QEC) decoders that achieve low logical error rates under real-time operating constraints. These constraints motivate heuristic decoding algorithms whose error-correction performance must be evaluated through large-scale simulation. High-throughput decoding accelerates this evaluation and the exploration of decoder parameters. Using multiple graphics processing units (GPUs) is a natural way to scale these simulations, but naively distributing syndrome batches introduces host-side preprocessing and output-collection overheads that limit scaling. To address these limitations, we extend the Pêlagos relay belief-propagation (Relay-BP) decoder with process-isolated orchestration, parallel host preprocessing, and shared-memory output. We evaluate both one-gross ($[[144,12,12]]$) and two-gross ($[[288,12,18]]$) codes in a…

papers_new.title: Quantum Material Generation via Coherent Hamiltonian Search
papers_new.abstract: Discovering new materials with targeted properties is a central goal of materials science, yet the space of candidates is vast. Data-driven generative models learn the distribution of known materials, but they extrapolate poorly, and a generated structure is not known to be stable. A material's properties follow from its Hamiltonian, and a quantum computer can calculate them from it. We introduce the quantum material generative algorithm (QMage), a coherent search, guided by the Hamiltonian, over crystalline configurations of atomic composition, unit cell structure, and atomic positions, for one whose calculated properties meet the targets to within a given error tolerance. The computation is a single coherent quantum circuit in which each configuration's Hamiltonian is block-encoded, its target eigenstate isolated and properties evaluated, and the satisfying configurations amplified by…

papers_new.title: Quasi-Cyclic Qudit Lifted Product Codes with Almost Linear Minimum Distance
papers_new.abstract: Quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes are a promising route to fault-tolerant quantum computation with low overhead, and qudits offer advantages over qubits including more efficient information representation, improved magic state distillation, and richer algebraic structure for code design. Asymptotically good QLDPC codes arise from the lifted product (LP) construction with non-abelian lifts, but cyclic lifts remain attractive in practice because the resulting quasi-cyclic codes have circulant structure that hardware decoders exploit, which matters especially for non-binary decoders with costly check node operations. We introduce a qudit generalization of the LP construction over cyclic group algebras, which extends hypergraph product and LP codes to arbitrary prime-power dimensions and yields quasi-cyclic qudit CSS codes for every stacking order. papers_new.title: Quantum-logic detection of rotationally inelastic collisions of single molecules
papers_new.abstract: Collisions between molecules govern chemical reactions and energy transfer across a range of different environments from interstellar space to the Earth's atmosphere. Despite their fundamental importance, molecular collisions have traditionally been studied through ensemble-averaged experiments which obscure the dynamics of individual scattering events on the quantum level. Probing single molecular collisions with quantum-state resolution has thus far remained a major experimental challenge. Here, we demonstrate a method for detecting individual rotationally inelastic collisions of single molecular ions with neutral atoms using quantum-logic techniques. We prepare individual trapped N$_2^+$ ions in their rotational ground state, subject them to a beam of helium atoms and detect isolated collision events through their effects on the motion of the trapped ions. papers_new.title: Quantum CSS codes: Decoder-aware multiobjective design and bound-certified selection
papers_new.abstract: Quantum error-correcting codes trade decoding reliability against the resources needed to measure their checks. We formulate Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) code design at fixed encoding resources as a decoder-aware multiobjective problem. The objectives are failure probability under sector-wise degenerate maximum-likelihood decoding and check weight, the minimum total weight of an independent pure-type generator basis. For independent bit- and phase-flip noise with perfect syndrome extraction, deterministic truncation bounds support selection under a failure-rate constraint. At a per-sector error probability of 0.01, the bounds certify that a code encoding two logical qubits into 40 physical qubits meets a failure-rate target of 0.001 at check weight 139. papers_new.title: Implementing rapid reset of superconducting qubits with on-chip dissipation
papers_new.abstract: Rapid and high-fidelity qubit reset is essential for quantum state initialization and quantum error correction. Conventional reset protocols for superconducting qubits often rely on dissipative elements connected to external circuitry, exposing qubits to thermal noise from higher-temperature environments. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a scalable approach to qubit reset and leakage removal over multiple transmon qubits using dedicated dissipation units comprising resonators coupled to on-chip resistive loads. This architecture provides Purcell protection while isolating the qubits from warmer external circuitry. We achieve a median reset time constant of approximately 48 ns for the $|g\rangle-|e\rangle$ transition, with an effective bath temperature of 30 mK. A 400-ns reset pulse yields residual excited-state populations of $0.29\%$ and $0.67\%$ for qubits initialized in…

papers_new.title: Circuit-aware protection against burst errors in lattice surgery
papers_new.abstract: Large-scale quantum computing will require logical operations protected against high-energy impacts that disturb many superconducting qubits at once. Gap engineering suppresses relaxation induced by these impacts, but protecting only a subset of qubits requires choosing where that protection is placed. During lattice surgery, measurements change as patches merge and split, exposing different ancillas and temporal boundaries to burst errors. Here we compare three static protection layouts for a simulated lattice-surgery CNOT, matching the numbers of protected ancillas and the X:Z check-type splits. At distance 9, protecting the check type measured during each merge reduces burst-induced excess risk by $38^{+6}_{-5}\%$ relative to a deep geometric band under correlated background matching, without giving the decoder the impact parameters. papers_new.title: A Compiler for Fault Tolerant Quantum Computing
papers_new.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) needs compiler intermediate representations (IRs) that preserve error-correcting-code choices, syndrome information, and non-Clifford resource requirements through analysis, simulation, and hardware lowering. We report practical experience building FTQC, an open-source Multi-Level Intermediate Representation (MLIR) dialect that makes logical qubits, syndromes, magic states, and Pauli frames typed static single assignment (SSA) values. Its error-correction-aware type system, two-level lowering design, and IR-resident resource analysis provide one inspectable pipeline to Open Quantum Assembly Language~3 (OpenQASM~3), the Quantum Intermediate Representation (QIR), Stim, and IQM hardware. papers_new.title: FusionQ: A Generic and Optimal Decoding Framework for Ultra-Low-Latency Quantum Error Correction
papers_new.abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) decoding has traditionally been organized around fixed decoding instances: a monolithic space-time detector error model (DEM), or a predetermined temporal window, is handed to a backend decoder after enough syndrome data has arrived. This paper presents FusionQ, a fusion decoding framework that changes this paradigm by deriving local decoding tasks from the observed syndrome and then fusing their results into a single global correction. Instead of forcing every shot through the same global or windowed problem, FusionQ builds open-boundary local DEMs around fired detector clusters and expands the corresponding footprints only when a local optimum uses virtual boundary errors. papers_new.title: The speed limit of gravitational entanglement and the cost of noise
papers_new.abstract: Is gravity quantum? A proposed test lets two small masses, each in a superposition of two places, become entangled through their mutual gravity. Gravity is weak, so the masses must stay coherent for seconds while random forces disturb them. Here we ask how fast gravity can entangle two masses, and what noise costs. Without noise we find the maximum rate exactly: it falls as the inverse cube of the separation, and two positions per mass achieve it. Above a noise level set by the masses and their separation, gravity's leading pull can be imitated by classical signals, and every strategy is limited to a rate falling at least as the inverse fourth power. Exact, continuous error correction shields the masses from noise but hides them from each other: the best rate falls as the inverse seventh power, and six positions on a hexagon come within 10% of it at large separation.

papers_new.title: Quantitative measurement of microwave power at millikelvin temperatures: Comparison between dispersively and directly coupled superconducting qubits
papers_new.abstract: The Rabi frequency of a two-level system is directly proportional to the electric field amplitude being incident on this system. Taking advantage of this relationship, it is possible to use two-level systems as quantitative sensors of electric fields. Here, we apply this concept to superconducting qubits and use them for quantitative measurement of microwave power at millikelvin temperatures. Our superconducting circuit design includes three transmon qubits directly coupled to the central microwave feedline and three transmon qubits coupled dispersively via readout resonators to the feedline. We compare both coupling schemes to assess their reliability for microwave power sensing. Further, we describe the modeling behind each power-sensing method, including an uncertainty estimation based upon repeated measurements. papers_new.title: Specifying & Verifying Quantum Error-Correcting Codes
papers_new.abstract: Building quantum computers is challenging due to the noise that affects qubits. Quantum error correction tackles noise by encoding information in quantum error-correcting (QEC) codes. These codes are often complex, increasingly found by computational search, presented in diverse formalisms with informal arguments, and hard to reason about algorithmically. Given that the rest of the quantum computing stack relies on a QEC code's properties for correct computation, we propose a formally verified foundation for QEC codes. We present QECLean, a Lean-based framework for formally specifying and verifying QEC codes. QECLean backs every claimed QEC-code property with a machine-checked proof, unifies the diverse presentations of codes in the literature through common abstractions, and makes new codes easy to specify. We present a new compositional technique, code combinators, for proving code…

papers_new.title: Metrological Channels Induced by Encrypted Quantum Cloning: Optimal-Probe Fisher-Information Broadcasting and Single-Use Operational Recovery
papers_new.abstract: Encrypted quantum cloning creates multiple individually inaccessible signal systems from which an unknown input state can be recovered by combining any selected signal with a shared quantum key. Here we study parameter estimation when a local sensing transformation is applied after encrypted cloning and before decryption. For the two-clone qubit protocol, a local Pauli rotation on one encrypted signal is shown to induce, after standard decryption, a parameter-dependent Pauli dephasing channel rather than a unitary rotation. We derive its Pauli-transfer representation and the corresponding quantum Fisher information (QFI) for arbitrary mixed qubit probes. We then distinguish raw QFI, which for an optimal decoded probe may remain simultaneously present in a decoded output and its complement, from decoder-accessible QFI, which is operationally single-use because a first decryption destroys…

papers_new.title: CSS circuits are ICM circuits without magic states
papers_new.abstract: Gidney and Jones recently introduced ``CSS circuits'', generated by $X$, $Z$, $\MX$, $\MZ$ and CNOT, and showed that they can be sampled with $O(1)$ work per gate. They suspected that the class had been seen before. We point out that it is, up to a normal form, the initialisation--CNOT--measurement (ICM) form introduced in 2015 for compiling fault-tolerant circuits, restricted to $\ket{0}$ and $\ket{+}$ initialisations. The ICM construction answers constructively their question about ``non-CSS-ness as a resource'': every Clifford$+T$ circuit compiles to a CSS circuit acting on $\ket{Y}$ and $\ket{A}$ input states.

papers_new.title: A Forward Bit Makes Error Correction Dispensable for Antidegradable Amplitude-Damping Channels
papers_new.abstract: Preserving a qubit usually relies on redundant encoding over many uses of a noisy channel. We prove that for antidegradable amplitude damping, one channel use with one forward classical bit matches or beats every forward-assisted or unassisted code with any number of uses. We then show that variational circuits learn to switch from error correction to classical assistance as damping grows, beating a dual-certified bound on all unassisted three-use codes and, relative to the best unassisted see-saw, extending storage time by up to 13% at entanglement fidelity down to 0.65.

papers_new.title: Hardware-Aware Realization of Deterministic Quantum-Walk Search on Complete Bipartite Graphs
papers_new.abstract: Complete bipartite graphs offer a canonical platform for deterministic quantum search with quadratic speedup. We report the first experimental realization of deterministic discrete-time quantum-walk search over complete bipartite graphs, enabled by high-fidelity operations and a dynamical-phase compensation scheme, using a digital gate-based processor rather than an evolution-based platform. By compiling the search circuits to the native gate set and square-lattice topology, we implement full-space encoding to realize instances of graph sizes $N = 4$ and $8$, with success probabilities of 97.6% and 70.8% for finding the marked vertex, respectively. We also realize resource-efficient exact instances up to size $N = 16$, the largest achieving 66% success probability. papers_new.title: Quantum Loading of Charge and Spin-Adapted MPS
papers_new.abstract: Matrix product states (MPS) are powerful classical representations of correlated quantum states, but loading a large bond dimension MPS can substantially increase the cost in fault-tolerant quantum algorithms. We develop a circuit for preparing a U(1)~$\times$~SU(2)-symmetric MPS directly from spin-adapted reduced tensors. Using Householder--LKS synthesis, the circuit prepares each symmetry-allowed reduced block and applies Clebsch--Gordan coefficients to recover the magnetic degrees of freedom, avoiding explicit loading of the corresponding unfolded dense tensors. The reduced-tensor data loading is dominant in cost. We benchmark $4 \times 4$ and $4 \times 6$ Fermi--Hubbard states and active-space models of \ce{[Fe2S2]^2-}, \ce{[Fe4S4]^2-}, and low- and high-spin cytochrome P450. At 15-bit rotation precision, the molecular benchmarks show $\sim 14\times$ to $54\times$ Toffoli…
papers_new.excerpt: Matrix product states (MPS) are powerful classical representations of correlated quantum states, but loading a large bond dimension MPS can substantially increase the cost in fault-tolerant quantum algorithms.

papers_new.title: Latency-Preserving Rewrites and Translation Validation for Dynamic Quantum Circuits
papers_new.abstract: A dynamic quantum circuit measures qubits during a run and chooses later operations from the outcomes. These branches make the qubits wait: the outcome must reach the classical controller, and the controller must decide. We present qlin, a compiler that reduces this waiting time. qlin moves operations out of branches without delaying the program, a property proved in Lean 4. For error-correction decoders, which branch on syndromes that are almost always zero, qlin compiles the likely syndromes into one multiway branch and keeps the original program for the rest. A cost model decides when a classically controlled gate should become a quantum-controlled gate instead. On all benchmarks, qlin checks that the compiled program computes what its source computes, and the checker is proved sound in Lean 4. papers_new.title: Dressed higher-form symmetries in mixed state quantum matter
papers_new.abstract: We describe how to construct emergent strong higher-form symmetries in mixed quantum states that act unitarily on Hilbert space. Our construction uses (quasi-)local recovery channels from quantum error correction to some nearby simple (stabilizer) model. We prove that when the recovery is done in an appropriate (deterministic) manner, the resulting operators continue to be unitary. When applied to operators acting on topologically non-trivial sub-manifolds (loops, surfaces), the resulting unitaries inherit the logical algebra of the fixed point model. More generally, the unitarity of the emergent symmetries allows one to define emergent excitations whose statistics follow those of the fixed point limit.
papers_new.excerpt: We describe how to construct emergent strong higher-form symmetries in mixed quantum states that act unitarily on Hilbert space.

papers_new.title: Quantum Dynamics of Dynamics
papers_new.abstract: Quantum channels (in discrete time) and Gorini--Kossakowski--Sudarshan--Lindblad (GKSL) master equations (in continuous time) are the central tools of open quantum systems, but they rest on memoryless approximations (Born, Markov, secular) that fail in many physically relevant settings, most notably non-Markovian dynamics. There, tracking the state alone is insufficient: interventions at intermediate times disturb the environment, so multi-time correlations carry physical information that the state evolution cannot capture. papers_new.abstract: Quantum Reinforcement Learning (QRL) using variational quantum circuits (VQCs) is constrained by fixed measurement protocols and hand-designed circuit ansätze. papers_new.abstract: The Quantum Singular Value Transformation (QSVT) is an algorithmic framework which encompasses a wide range of problems, including Hamiltonian dynamics, ground state preparation, Gibbs state preparation, amplitude amplification, and matrix inversion. papers_new.title: Metamorphic Testing of Quantum Software based on Stabilizer States
papers_new.abstract: A major challenge in quantum computing is to systematically check if a quantum program implements its desired functionality. For classical programs, testing is widely used; each test case comprises a pair of sample input and expected output to be compared with the actual output. To increase the number of test cases, however, one has to solve the test-oracle problem: for each additional test input one has to know the correct output. Metamorphic testing tackles this problem by utilizing metamorphic relations between input and output domains to automatically derive new test cases from existing ones. papers_new.title: Agentic AI for Discovering Fault-Tolerant Quantum Circuits
papers_new.abstract: Scaling quantum computing toward practical quantum advantage is currently limited by the efficiency of circuits that operate on information encoded by quantum error-correcting codes. papers_new.title: Beyond Blossom: Accelerating MWPM Decoding for Surface Codes With Local Predecoding and Architecture-Aware Optimizations
papers_new.abstract: Minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM) is widely used to decode surface codes, but its computational cost increases with code distance. We present Beyond Blossom, a state-of-the-art CPU-based MWPM decoder for surface codes. It combines algorithmic optimization through local predecoding, architecture-aware optimization, and pipeline-wide parallelism to reduce matching workload and execution overhead while preserving MWPM optimality. Across rotated surface codes with distances 9-33 and circuit-level physical error rates of 0.05%-0.3%, on a single CPU core, Beyond Blossom achieves a 4.23$\times$ geometric-mean speedup and up to 5.58$\times$ speedup over Sparse Blossom in PyMatching. At distance 33 and a physical error rate of 0.1%, with 8 CPU cores, decoding a block of 33 measurement rounds takes 21.40 $μ$s on average, equivalent to 0.65 $μ$s per round.

papers_new.title: Transfer-Matrix Calculus for Infinite Matrix Product States
papers_new.abstract: Long-range interactions, from the Coulomb repulsion between electrons to the power-law interactions of trapped ions and Rydberg atoms, are widespread in quantum many-body physics.
